Policy Name: Cigna ACDF (CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion)
Referred Sections: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF)

Required findings: Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.) AND unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability

ANY of the following: dermatomal sensory deficit, motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness), reflex changes, shoulder abduction relief sign, nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver), or unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings

MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and is caused by ANY of the following: herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation), synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst, central/lateral/foraminal stenosis, or osteophytes

Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks; provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks; or epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery

Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders) AND documentation of nicotine-free status (never-smoker OR refrained from smoking, smokeless tobacco, and nicotine replacement therapy for at least six (6) weeks prior to surgery validated by objective cotinine testing within normal range)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) > Radiculopathy (TOC: S9.1.1)

Required findings: ANY of the following: upper/lower extremity weakness, numbness, or pain; fine motor dysfunction (buttoning, handwriting, clumsiness of hands); gait disturbance; new-onset bowel or bladder dysfunction; or frequent falls

ANY of the following: grip and release test, ataxic gait, hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, Babinski sign, tandem walking test demonstrating ataxia, inverted brachial radial reflex, increased muscle tone or spasticity, clonus, or myelopathic hand

MRI/CT shows findings that are concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and are caused by EITHER of the following: cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis
N/A (Conservative management trial not explicitly required for Myelopathy in this section)
N/A (Behavioral/nicotine criteria not explicitly listed in Myelopathy subsection, but general policy application may vary; strictly based on text, only Radiculopathy lists these)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-601.4: Initial Primary Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) > Myelopathy (TOC: S9.1.2)

Non-Indications: Radiculopathy cases where the patient has not demonstrated less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least two of the specified conservative treatments (analgesics/NSAIDs/gabapentinoids, exercise, or injections) for six weeks, unless contraindicated
Radiculopathy cases where MRI/CT does not show neural structure compression concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings

Radiculopathy cases where the patient has unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)
Radiculopathy cases where the patient is not nicotine-free (smoker or has used smokeless tobacco/nicotine replacement therapy within 6 weeks of surgery without valid negative cotinine testing)
Myelopathy cases where MRI/CT findings are not concordant with symptoms and physical exam findings or are not caused by cervical spinal cord compression or cervical spinal stenosis
Important criteria & exceptions: For Radiculopathy, conservative management requirements can be waived if contraindicated

Nicotine-free status for Radiculopathy can be established by being a never-smoker OR by refraining from all nicotine products for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery, validated by objective cotinine testing (serum, urinary, or saliva) within normal range

For Radiculopathy, physical exam findings may include 'unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity without concordant objective physical exam findings' as a qualifying finding, provided other criteria are met
Documentation required: Plain x-rays of the cervical spine including flexion/extension lateral views
MRI or CT reports showing neural structure compression or spinal cord compression/stenosis concordant with symptoms and exam

Records of conservative management including prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs, provider-directed exercise program, or epidural steroid injections/selective nerve root blocks for at least 6 weeks (for Radiculopathy)
Objective cotinine testing results (serum, urinary, or saliva) verified as within normal range (for Radiculopathy if not a never-smoker)
Documentation of absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (for Radiculopathy)
